_what_this_is: Per network caption rules. One post goes out as several captions, one shaped for each place it lands. Copy this to specs/platforms.json and correct anything that looks wrong for your accounts.
_read_this_first: Platform limits change and this file is a snapshot of what was believed true when it was written, never a live reading. Every entry carries a confidence. Anything marked 'verify' should be checked against the platform before you trust it. adapt_caption.py prints that warning on every run for a reason.

instagram.confidence: high on the 2200 and on links being unclickable in a caption. The 125 is where the 'more' fold usually falls and moves with the app.

tiktok.confidence: verify. The caption limit was 150 for years and was raised. The lead is short because the caption sits over the video and competes with it.

threads.confidence: high on 500 and on links working. Threads has one topic tag rather than a hashtag block, which is why this is 1.

pinterest.confidence: medium. Pinterest reads descriptions as search text, so plain words beat tags and a handle means nothing to it.

youtube.confidence: high on the description allowance. The 100 is the Shorts title, which is the part that actually gets read.

facebook.confidence: medium. The hard limit is far higher and irrelevant. Hashtags do close to nothing here, so they come off.
